alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines state EFV frequently causes neuropsychiatric effects like insomnia and vivid dreams, typically within the first 2-6 weeks of therapy. The patient has been on an EFV-based regimen since February 2024 and presents with poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. This is a known side effect of EFV. However, the symptoms are occurring long after the typical onset period, suggesting a persistent or late-onset toxicity. The patient denies suicidal ideation, which is a more severe concern associated with EFV.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess severity of CNS symptoms and consider reporting the adverse event. Evaluate need for regimen switch if symptoms are intolerable.

alerts.title: Missing viral load monitoring
alerts.message: The patient's last viral load test was on 2025-08-10, showing 60 copies/mL. This is over 5 months (165 days) old at the time of the current visit on 2026-01-22. Regular viral load monitoring is essential to assess treatment efficacy and adherence. There is no record of a viral load test being ordered at today's visit. The absence of a recent result creates an information gap regarding current virologic control.

evidence.recommended_action: Order a viral load test today to assess current treatment response.
